Construct a Tracks from a data.frame or file(s)

Source: R/loaders.R
read_tracks.Rd

Construct a Tracks from a data.frame or file(s)

Usage

read_tracks(
  x,
  mapping = list(id = NULL, time = NULL, x = NULL, y = NULL, angle = NULL, weight = NULL),
  angle_unit = c("radians", "degrees", "auto"),
  time_type = c("auto", "posix", "seconds", "frames"),
  tz = "UTC",
  fps = NULL,
  normalize_xy = FALSE,
  origin = NULL,
  radius = NULL,
  dialect = NULL,
  dialect_args = list(),
  read_opts = list(delim = NULL, decimal = NULL, sheet = NULL),
  mutate = NULL,
  keep = NULL,
  drop = NULL,
  id_from_filename = TRUE,
  validate = TRUE,
  format = NULL,
  id_collision = c("error", "namespace"),
  on_invalid = c("error", "drop")
)

Arguments

x

data.frame, file path, or character vector of file paths

mapping

named list for column mapping: id, time, x, y, angle, weight. Any missing will be guessed when possible.

angle_unit

"radians","degrees", or "auto" to guess from values

time_type

one of "auto","posix","seconds","frames". Numeric time is taken to be a frame index unless `time_type = "seconds"` (or the column is a duration): seconds are recorded as such in the Tracks metadata (`time_unit`), so [elapsed_seconds()] and the kinematics use them directly, with no frame rate.

tz

Time zone of timestamps that carry none (default "UTC") in a delimited or Excel file `read_tracks()` reads itself, and in a text column of a data frame; a bare date is midnight in `tz`. A wall-clock time that does not exist in `tz` (the hour skipped when clocks go forward) is an error. A timestamp marked `Z` is UTC whatever `tz` is, a date-time column of a data frame keeps its instants, and `tz` does not reach a file read by a dialect.

fps

Frames-per-second. Required when time_type = "frames" (the time column is kept as a raw frame index). When a single finite positive value is supplied and the time column is frame-indexed, it is stored as the Tracks capture frame rate (see [frame_rate()]); [elapsed_seconds()] then performs the frame -> seconds conversion once, on demand, so kinematics and the app adopt it automatically without converting twice.

normalize_xy

FALSE (default) keeps (x,y) as supplied. TRUE independently centres each trajectory on its own bounding-box midpoint and scales it to the unit circle – shape-preserving only, NOT calibration (it does not preserve bearing from a fixed arena origin). See [tracks()] for the full explanation.

origin, radius

Optional fixed unit-circle calibration forwarded to [tracks()]: `origin = c(x, y)` centre and positive scalar `radius` in raw coordinate units. Supplied together, they map every trajectory uniformly via `(xy - origin) / radius`, preserving bearings from the origin. Mutually exclusive with `normalize_xy = TRUE`.

dialect

optional registered dialect name. The dialect reads `x` itself (`read_tracks()` does not parse the file first) and is called once per file when `x` holds several paths. See [register_loader_dialect()].

dialect_args

named list of extra arguments forwarded to the dialect function (e.g. list(bodypart = c("head","thorax")))

read_opts

list of file-reading overrides: `delim` (field separator), `decimal` (decimal mark), and `sheet` (Excel worksheet name or number). Any `NULL` element is auto-detected. Defaults to all-auto.

mutate

list of transformations applied after reading (named functions or formulas)

keep

extra columns to retain besides the mapped ones and those a dialect produces (NULL = none). All other columns are dropped; a name that is not in the data is ignored without a message.

drop

drop these columns after mapping

id_from_filename

if TRUE and id missing, derive id from file stem when reading multiple files

validate

Deprecated and ignored: `Tracks` invariants are always checked. Any value but `TRUE` warns.

format

Optional loader format name or list spec registered via [register_loader_format()]

id_collision

how to handle a trajectory id that appears under more than one source file during a multi-file import: `"error"` (default) stops with a message naming the colliding id(s) and files; `"namespace"` rewrites every id to `paste0(file_stem, "::", id)` so ids are unique per file. Has no effect on single-file or data.frame input.

on_invalid

How to handle rows whose x/y coordinates are missing or non-finite: "error" (default) aborts with a radiatR_invalid_rows condition listing the affected rows and ids; "drop" removes them and signals a radiatR_dropped_rows warning with the same payload. It covers nothing else: a missing time, id or weight is an error either way, and so is a malformed value (see "Malformed values").

Value

Tracks

Time units from a dialect

A dialect that knows the unit of its time column says so, and under the default `time_type = "auto"` that decides how the column is read: TrackMate `POSITION_T` (when the version 7 units row gives seconds), ToxTrac `Time (sec)`, idtracker.ai `seconds` and TRex `time` are seconds, and need no `fps`; `FRAME`/`frame` columns, the DeepLabCut frame index and SLEAP `frame_idx` are frames. `ethovision` (`Trial time`, or `Recording time` through `time_col`) and `anymaze` (`Time`, a duration) declare seconds; an `ethovision` data frame's time is taken as seconds (EthoVision writes no other unit), and a file's units row is checked. A contrary explicit `time_type` stops with a `radiatR_time_type_mismatch` error, as do files of one import that disagree.

Masked points

The `deeplabcut`, `sleap`, `ethovision` and `anymaze` dialects take each position from one or more points (bodyparts, nodes, body points; ANY-maze's centre point alone). EthoVision writes `-` and ANY-maze an empty cell for a sample with no position; neither has scores, thresholds, or for `anymaze` a `partial` argument. A point is masked in a frame when its coordinates are missing or not finite, when its score (likelihood) is 0, or when a threshold is given (`dialect_args = list(likelihood_min = )` for DeepLabCut, `score_min` for SLEAP) and its score is missing or below it. A frame with a masked point has no position, unless `dialect_args = list(partial = "mean")` asks for the score-weighted mean of the points that remain. The dialect never removes a row: frames without a position meet `on_invalid` like any other missing coordinate.

What was masked is reported in one message (class `radiatR_attrition`) and kept in the `attrition` element of the Tracks metadata: a data frame with one row per source file and point, giving the rows in which the point was masked (`masked`), the rows read from that file (`frames`), the rows left without a position (`frames_no_position`), and the threshold and `partial` setting used. `c()` row-binds these records; a subset keeps the whole record of its load, so recombining subsets of one load repeats it.

Ids

An id is a label, not a measurement. In a delimited file the id column (the one named in `mapping`, or any column named `id`, `track`, `trajectory`, `animal` or `subject`) is kept as the text in the file wherever reading it as numbers would merge ids that are written differently: `1.1` and `1.10`, `1` and `1.0`, `01` and `1`. Ids that read as distinct numbers stay numbers. Where the delimited files of one import do not agree on the type of the id column, the ids of each file are the text in that file. Ids that are numbers in every file are compared as numbers across files (see `id_collision`). A data frame and an Excel or Arrow file keep the types they come with. An `anymaze` file is read as text, so the column its `id_col` names keeps its text. For `ethovision`, `id_col` applies to a data frame only (a file is one track, id `"1"`). Not covered: an id column that another dialect is pointed to by an argument of its own (its ids may still be merged).

Malformed values

A cell in an x, y, angle, weight or time column that is present but does not parse (`"oops"`, `"1,5"`, a stray header or units row) stops the load with a `radiatR_malformed_values` error, a subclass of `radiatR_invalid_rows`. Its `columns`, `rows`, `values`, `source` and `dialect` fields name the column, the data rows (counted from the first row after the header, within its own file in a multi-file import), the offending strings, the file and the dialect. Such a value is never dropped or turned into `NA`. Blank cells and `NA` are missing values; `nan` and `inf` are read as such. Files are read with no digit-grouping mark, so `1,5` is malformed unless `read_opts = list(decimal = ",")` says the comma is the decimal mark. Where it is, a value holding a `.` is malformed in turn, since `1.234` could as well be 1234. A semicolon-separated file is taken to use decimal commas unless its first lines show decimal points and no decimal comma (`1.5` or `0.125`, which cannot be digit grouping, or the fraction of a duration such as `0:00:00.320`); `read_opts = list(decimal = ".")` says so outright.

Every built-in dialect checks its source columns the same way, before any reshaping, so the error names the header as the program wrote it and the row of the file's table. A missing or non-finite position found afterwards (see `on_invalid`) is still counted in the rows of the table the dialect returns, which for a wide format is the reshaped one. ANY-maze writes time as a duration (`0:01:02.500`), read as seconds; a cell that is not one is malformed.

A time column given as text must hold either numbers throughout or timestamps in one layout throughout: `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD` (with `-` or `/`), or ISO 8601 `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS` with an optional `Z` for UTC. A bare date beside date-times is midnight.
